solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Extra crop ruined at the farm

indicators.note: what is ruined is wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of AT THE FARM rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer's second harvest has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: "At the farm" reads as a setting for the ruin, but it is the raw material. An aftermath is literally a second growth of grass after mowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftermath originally meant a second mowing, the extra crop that grows after the first cut.

clue.text: Nothing left? That's OK

definitions.meaning: if everything is on the right, nothing is left
an everyday phrase of reassurance, meaning fine

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off having run out of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: "Left" looks like remaining, but it is the direction: if it is all right, none is left.
explanation.definitionFit: All right is a standard way of saying something is OK.

clue.text: Made adjustments to first of Titian's nude works

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new order
take the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An art restorer has touched up one of Titian's nudes.
explanation.walkthrough: "Works" looks like paintings, a natural noun after Titian, but it is a verb telling you to rework NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune something is to make fine adjustments to it.

clue.text: Tries again with a learner in practice session

parts.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it again
L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A driving instructor has another go with a student.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tries" suggests attempts, but it is the legal sense: to rehear a case is to try it again.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a practice run before a performance is the standard sense.

clue.text: Incomplete expression of regret involving piece in annual publication

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
the outer word takes the other inside it

parts.note: ALACK, an old cry of regret, without its last letter
a chess or draughts piece is a man

explanation.surface: A half-hearted apology about an article in a yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Alack is an archaic exclamation like alas. "Piece" means a game piece, not a written article.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is published once a year.

clue.text: Hamlet's first speech mainly for his friend

indicators.note: take the first letter of Hamlet
most of the word, so drop its last letter

explanation.surface: Hamlet's opening speech is mostly addressed to his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface stays in Hamlet's world, so the answer hides in plain sight: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play, Horatio is Hamlet's closest friend.

clue.text: Examination that involves studying books

parts.note: the surface pushes a school exam; the setter means an inspection
the books are account books, a firm's financial records

explanation.surface: A student's exam requires reading textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The books are account books, not reading matter, and the examination is of them rather than of a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of an organisation's accounts, or books.

clue.text: Like part of Greece that's reached by final flight

definitions.meaning: Attica is the region round Athens; its adjective describes things from there
a flight of stairs: the last one leads to the room under the roof

explanation.surface: A traveller lands in part of Greece on the last plane.
explanation.walkthrough: "Flight" suggests an aeroplane, but it is a flight of stairs; the top one leads to the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes Attica or Athens; an attic is the room under the roof, up the last stairs.

clue.text: Send daily broadcast? Do that and be damned

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer as an act that damns you rather than naming it

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio producer is told that a daily show is a damnable idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as a description: in Christian teaching, committing a deadly sin damns the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven deadly sins are those said to lead to damnation.

clue.text: Harden after short time in occupation

indicators.note: the harden word comes after the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
enure is a variant spelling of inure, to harden

explanation.surface: Someone becomes toughened soon after starting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: ENURE is the less common spelling of inure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding or occupation of a post or property.

clue.text: Have some meal, uncharged? Never

indicators.note: part of the following words

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at the idea of a free meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue plays on the saying "there's no such thing as a free lunch": a meal uncharged never happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying insists that a lunch at no charge never truly exists.

clue.text: Book two for novelist

parts.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament
twain is an old word for two

explanation.surface: Someone orders a second copy of a book for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Book" is a book of the Bible, not a volume or a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the American novelist who wrote Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Shy and introspective, so expelled? Just the opposite

parts.note: breath expelled is drawn out; the opposite is drawn in, written as one word with the parts swapped

explanation.surface: A shy person is described, then corrected: not thrown out but the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: "Expelled" suggests a school, but think of breath: breathed out is drawn out, so the opposite is drawn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn means withdrawn into oneself, reserved and introspective.

clue.text: Equipment right for undertaker?

definitions.note: undertaker here means one who undertakes or takes on a task, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A funeral director needs the proper gear.
explanation.walkthrough: An undertaker usually buries the dead; here it is someone who undertakes, or tackles, a job.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tackles a job is one who undertakes it.

clue.text: This rhapsodic introduction of Ravel's transported musician

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word
carried off, so the letters move to new places

explanation.surface: A performer is carried away by the opening of a Ravel rhapsody.
explanation.walkthrough: "Transported" looks like rapture at the music, but it moves the letters of THIS RHAPSODIC plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpsichordist is a musician who plays the harpsichord.

clue.text: Is a modern broadcast haphazardly set up?

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a modern broadcast is put together carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: to randomise is to arrange by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To randomise is to set things out in a haphazard, random order.

clue.text: Spoke about one number overturning analysis of problem

indicators.note: the spoke word goes round the others
in a down clue, turning over reverses the order

explanation.surface: Someone talks of a single figure upsetting a problem analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: "One number" looks like a single figure, but it is one plus a song. The whole assembly reads from the bottom up, so the answer opens with the verb backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the identification of a problem by analysing its signs.

clue.text: Supply key leads in careless fashion

indicators.note: the key letter goes in front

parts.note: supply as the adverb of supple, which is lithely

explanation.surface: Someone hands over keys and cables without care.
explanation.walkthrough: "Supply" is not provide but the adverb from supple, pronounced SUP-lee.
explanation.definitionFit: To act blithely is to act casually, without care or concern.

clue.text: What ex-pat might view as something that divides us from Europe

definitions.meaning: a Briton abroad might watch a TV channel in English

definitions.text: something that divides us from Europe
definitions.meaning: the sea strait between England and France

explanation.surface: A Briton abroad looks back across the water at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a television channel in English; the second is the strait between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Channel is the sea separating Britain from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Artist superior to Constable, reportedly

indicators.note: as it is reported, spoken aloud

parts.note: a police sergeant ranks above a constable

explanation.surface: A critic claims some painter outranks John Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the painter John Constable, which suits "artist", but it is the lowest police rank. John Singer Sargent was a portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a celebrated American portrait artist.

clue.text: Topical reforms in American political scene

indicators.note: forms again, in a new order

explanation.surface: Current reforms are under way in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: "Reforms" fits politics so well it reads as a noun, but it is the verb that rearranges TOPICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capitol in Washington is where the US Congress meets.

clue.text: The writer ultimately diminished great singer as tragic high-flier

indicators.note: cut at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
CARUSO, the great tenor, without his last letter

explanation.surface: A writer ends up belittling a famous singer as a doomed star.
explanation.walkthrough: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian tenor. Icarus flew too near the sun and fell.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew so high that his wax wings melted.

clue.text: Trumpet introducing bit of music — it makes a forceful entry

indicators.note: the trumpet word comes first, bringing in the next

parts.note: to trumpet a success is to crow about it
a bar is a short section of music

explanation.surface: A fanfare announces a dramatic arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: "Trumpet" looks like the instrument beside the music, but it is the verb meaning to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is used to force doors and windows open.

clue.text: Hairstyle worn by sailor and his colleague

indicators.note: the hairstyle is put on around the sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor and a shipmate both sport the same hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: "His colleague" points back to the sailor: a bosun is a ship's officer, a fellow seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosun, or boatswain, works alongside the ordinary sailors on a ship.

clue.text: Piece of jewellery author and poet shortened

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A writer and a poet cut down a necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: "Author" is the verb, to write, which is to pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: this jewellery hangs, and its name comes from the Latin for hanging.

clue.text: Friend from Europe with another on journey

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: another friend from Europe: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A European pal travels with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: "Another" leans on the definition: another friend from Europe is the French AMI. Amigo is Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain translation: the word is Spanish, and Spain is in Europe.

clue.text: Once more check and control cult holding power

indicators.note: the cult word holds the power letter inside

explanation.surface: An inspector checks again and curbs a sect's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: "Check" and "control" sit side by side as if meaning the same, but only the first is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix re- means again, so this is an inspection repeated.

clue.text: Sound of delightful musical sequence

indicators.note: the answer sounds like the word

explanation.surface: Someone admires a lovely piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as praise for music, which neatly hides that "sound of" is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a set of musical movements played in sequence.

clue.text: Republican welcomed by gun firm

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside, so the gun takes in the Republican

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A gun company takes in a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: "Firm" looks like a company to go with the gun, but it is the adjective meaning strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the strict sense, as of a parent who will not give way.

clue.text: Politician of considerable stature swallowing second dubious account

indicators.note: the politician phrase takes the letter inside

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A prominent politician falls for a questionable tale.
explanation.walkthrough: "Of considerable stature" suggests importance, but it is literal height. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an account too far-fetched to believe.
